title: Exercise workflow recovery, cancellation, and cleanup races
body:
Exercise concurrent recovery and abandonment, cancellation/claim serialization, and cleanup/recovery races using independent database connections. Include browser recovery through shared operator services.

Acceptance criteria:
- Repeated recovery requests retain one audit mutation and reject conflicts.
- Cancellation cannot start unrun work after hold release.
- Cleanup preserves parent results and replay lineage while recovery is possible.

Source: docs/archive/development/2026-10/evidence/p1-local-2026-10-23.md (Open acceptance work). Reconcile with current code and existing issues before implementation.

title: Bound whole-operation deadlines and sweep fairness
body:
Review whole-operation database and transport deadlines across adapters. Exercise slow SQL, delayed transport, and noisy routes using the existing deadline and sweep metrics.

Acceptance criteria:
- A run stays within its invocation budget, including database waits and callbacks.
- Slow work cannot starve other routes.
- Connection timeout settings are restored on success and failure.

title: Run shared database contracts across the declared engine matrix
body:
Use the existing compatibility workflow and shared fixtures to exercise supported engine/version/driver combinations. Retain versioned results for lifecycle, rollback, deduplication, claims, fencing, workflow recovery, and connection restoration.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fresh core/workflow migrations apply on each selected engine.
- Concurrency uses independent connections or processes.
- Results identify exact Python, server, driver, and dependency versions.

title: Verify consumer images with native database drivers
body:
Build consumer images from locked requirements for the experimental engine extras and exercise settings, secret precedence, TLS, and supplied-database connectivity.

Acceptance criteria:
- Images identify immutable digests and hashed dependency inputs.
- Native-driver imports and application task execution work inside each image.
- Configuration and secret refresh behavior are covered without exposing credentials.

title: Exercise installed artifact, upgrade, and browser compatibility
body:
Run the existing installed-artifact checks across declared Python, driver, and minimum/latest dependency combinations. Include workflows enabled/disabled, package assets, and the browser operator journey.

Acceptance criteria:
- Wheel and sdist run outside the source checkout.
- Queued/held work survives the supported additive rollout and rollback scenario.
- Reports identify artifact hashes and exact dependencies.

title: Run disposable service integration and operator drills
body:
Use the example tooling in an explicitly selected disposable account for queue routing, scheduled recovery, forced termination, initialization failure/DLQ/hold, provider response loss, database disruption, and rollout/rollback exercises.

Acceptance criteria:
- Verify durable task and business outcomes, not just invocation success.
- Check permissions, log navigation, credential refresh, and delivered alarm notifications.
- Record resource identities and confirm cleanup.

title: Measure workload capacity and regional usage costs
body:
Use the example workload and capacity tools to measure burst, sustained, and outage recovery behavior at the declared concurrency budgets.

Acceptance criteria:
- Retain latency, outcomes, queue/backlog, database sessions, and wait series.
- Apply explicit success thresholds to each workload class.
- Retain sourced, dated regional pricing and observed usage inputs.

title: Rehearse maintainer setup and exact-artifact release workflow
body:
Review branch protections, required checks, protected environments, and OIDC configuration using the maintainer guides. Rehearse candidate verification and a clean developer installation journey.

Acceptance criteria:
- Candidate reports identify the same source and wheel/sdist hashes.
- Verify install, migrate, both routes, diagnosis, recovery, and cleanup from written instructions.
- Keep publication a separate action; do not expand this personal prototype into a production support commitment.
